reason: This passage from Exodus 1:8-12 describes a new Pharaoh expressing concerns about the growing Israelite population to his people and proposing oppressive measures. The Egyptian people subsequently comply with the Pharaoh's directives by placing taskmasters over the Israelites and building storage cities. The only antagonism explicitly described in the text is between the Egyptians and the Israelites (הִנֵּ֗ה עַ֚ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל - 'the Israelite people are numerous and mighty'; וַיָּקֻ֕צוּ - 'they loathed the Israelites'). There is no evidence of the Egyptian people being antagonistic toward their leader; rather, they appear to be cooperating with his policies.
story: The Pharaoh turns on the Hebrews
